edits.before: We do this for two deterministic sampled models. One adjusts a broadcast by the gradient of a target response using an old report. The other first advances a relaxing plant, then applies a collective response to the newly observed mismatch. This apparently small timing and controller choice changes the stability calculation and the nonlinear result. We then replace a flat detector bank by exact, specified majority trees, and finally attach an independently defined actuator. The contribution is the resulting chain of calculations: from a microscopic vote to its derivative, from that derivative to the appropriate full-loop boundary, and from an admitted architecture to a reachable intervention within budget. The paper supplies its own proofs and numerical method. No inference requires an earlier version of the argument.

edits.before: The positive conclusion is therefore constructive. Hierarchy can be designed as a response transformation and tested against a controller-specific stability condition. Exact product trees make that test finite and reproducible: the \(243\)-leaf example gains an admissible subcritical architecture, while the \(729\)-leaf example does not. Reachability and minimum-norm control then price a declared intervention on a separately specified chain. These calculations replace an unrestricted depth prescription by the feasible set in Eq.~\eqref{hrec:eq:feasibility}.
